categories.title: HTTP servers and networking
categories.summary: HTTP servers, TCP/UDP sockets and the fetch client built into the Bun global.

categories.title: Files and paths
categories.summary: Reading, writing, streaming, memory-mapping and globbing files, plus URL/path conversion.

categories.title: Process and environment
categories.summary: Command-line arguments, environment variables, working directory, executable lookup and timing helpers.

categories.title: Runtime control
categories.summary: Version information, garbage-collection control, native secrets, cron scheduling and compiled-executable state.

categories.title: Bun Shell
categories.summary: Cross-platform shell scripting through tagged template literals.

categories.title: Child processes
categories.summary: Spawning children synchronously or asynchronously and driving them through a pseudo-terminal.

categories.title: Hashing and security
categories.summary: Fast hashing, cryptographic digests, password hashing, UUIDs and CSRF tokens.

categories.title: Compression and archives
categories.summary: gzip, deflate and zstd compression plus tar archive creation and extraction.

categories.title: Text and encoding utilities
categories.summary: Object inspection, deep equality, HTML escaping and ANSI-aware string measurement and slicing.

categories.title: Databases and object storage
categories.summary: SQL clients for SQLite and Postgres, a Redis client, and S3-compatible object storage.

categories.title: Parsing and serialization
categories.summary: Parsers and stringifiers for TOML, YAML, JSON5, JSONL, XML and Markdown.

categories.title: Build and tooling
categories.summary: Bundling, transpiling, module resolution, plugins and native FFI bindings.

apis.name: Bun.serve
apis.summary: Starts an HTTP(S) server with a fetch handler and optional WebSocket, static-route and TLS options. Returns a Server whose url, protocol, port, hostname and stop() let you inspect and shut it down.
apis.signature: Bun.serve<WebSocketData = undefined, R extends string = never>(options: Bun.Serve.Options<WebSocketData, R>): Bun.Server<WebSocketData>

apis.name: Bun.listen
apis.summary: Creates a TCP or Unix-domain socket server and invokes the socket handlers for open, data, close and error events. The returned listener exposes port, hostname, reload() and stop().
apis.signature: Bun.listen<Data = undefined>(options: Bun.TCPSocketListenOptions<Data>): Bun.TCPSocketListener<Data>

apis.name: Bun.connect
apis.summary: Opens a TCP or TLS client connection and resolves once the socket is connected. Data, close, connect and error handlers are passed in the options object.
apis.signature: Bun.connect<Data = undefined>(options: Bun.TCPSocketConnectOptions<Data>): Promise<Bun.Socket<Data>>

apis.name: Bun.udpSocket
apis.summary: Binds a UDP socket for sending and receiving datagrams, optionally connected to a fixed remote address. Resolves to a socket with send(), close(), port and address.
apis.signature: Bun.udpSocket<DataBinaryType extends Bun.BinaryType = "buffer">(options: Bun.udp.SocketOptions<DataBinaryType>): Promise<Bun.udp.Socket<DataBinaryType>>

apis.name: Bun.fetch
apis.summary: Bun's implementation of the WHATWG fetch API, re-exported on the Bun namespace. It adds Bun-specific request options such as proxy, TLS settings and connection reuse.
apis.signature: Bun.fetch(input: string | URL | Request, init?: BunFetchRequestInit): Promise<Response>

apis.name: Bun.file
apis.summary: Creates a lazy BunFile reference to a path, a file descriptor or in-memory bytes. The file is not read until you call text(), json(), bytes(), stream() or similar.
apis.signature: Bun.file(path: string | URL, options?: BlobPropertyBag): BunFile

apis.name: Bun.write
apis.summary: Writes a string, typed array, Blob, Response, ReadableStream or Archive to a path, BunFile or S3 file. Resolves to the number of bytes written and creates parent directories by default.
apis.signature: Bun.write(destination: BunFile | PathLike, input: Blob | BufferSource | string | ReadableStream, options?: { mode?: number; createPath?: boolean }): Promise<number>

apis.name: Bun.stdin
apis.summary: The process standard input as a BunFile. Read it with text(), json(), bytes(), stream() or arrayBuffer().
apis.signature: Bun.stdin: BunFile
apis.example:
const input = await Bun.stdin.text();
console.log("stdin length:", input.length);

apis.name: Bun.stdout
apis.summary: The process standard output as a BunFile. Supports write() and file descriptor access.
apis.signature: Bun.stdout: BunFile
apis.example:
Bun.stdout.write("hello from stdout\n");
console.log("wrote to stdout");

apis.name: Bun.stderr
apis.summary: The process standard error as a BunFile, useful for diagnostics that should bypass stdout.
apis.signature: Bun.stderr: BunFile
apis.example:
Bun.stderr.write("something went wrong\n");
console.log("logged to stderr");

apis.name: Bun.mmap
apis.summary: Memory-maps a file into a Uint8Array without copying its contents. Currently supported on Linux and macOS, not on Windows.
apis.signature: Bun.mmap(path: string, opts?: Bun.MMapOptions): Uint8Array
apis.example:
const map = Bun.mmap("./hello.txt");
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(map));

apis.name: Bun.Glob
apis.summary: Matches file paths against glob patterns. scan() and scanSync() walk a directory tree, and match() tests a single path string.
apis.signature: class Bun.Glob { constructor(pattern: string); scan(optionsOrCwd?: string | Bun.GlobScanOptions): AsyncIterableIterator<string>; scanSync(optionsOrCwd?: string | Bun.GlobScanOptions): IterableIterator<string>; match(str: string): boolean }

apis.name: Bun.fileURLToPath
apis.summary: Converts a file: URL into a platform-native filesystem path.
apis.signature: Bun.fileURLToPath(url: URL | string): string
apis.example:
const path = Bun.fileURLToPath(Bun.pathToFileURL(Bun.main));
console.log(path === Bun.main);

apis.name: Bun.pathToFileURL
apis.summary: Converts a filesystem path into a file: URL object.
apis.signature: Bun.pathToFileURL(path: string): URL
apis.example:
const url = Bun.pathToFileURL(Bun.main);
console.log(url.protocol, url.href.startsWith("file://"));

apis.name: Bun.argv
apis.summary: The raw process arguments: the Bun executable, the script path, and any flags passed to the script.
apis.signature: Bun.argv: string[]
apis.example:
console.log(Bun.argv[0]);
console.log(Bun.argv.slice(2));

apis.name: Bun.env
apis.summary: The process environment variables as a mutable object. Values are strings or undefined and assignments affect the child processes Bun spawns.
apis.signature: Bun.env: Record<string, string | undefined>

apis.name: Bun.cwd
apis.summary: The absolute path of the process working directory as a string. Present on the Bun global in this runtime even though it is not yet listed on the reference page.
apis.signature: Bun.cwd: string
apis.example:
console.log(Bun.cwd);
console.log(Bun.cwd === process.cwd());

apis.name: Bun.main
apis.summary: The absolute path of the entrypoint script that launched the process, or a synthetic path when code is evaluated with -e.
apis.signature: Bun.main: string
apis.example:
console.log(Bun.main);
console.log(import.meta.main);

apis.name: Bun.which
apis.summary: Locates an executable on PATH, the same way the which command does, and returns its absolute path or null.
apis.signature: Bun.which(command: string, options?: Bun.WhichOptions): string | null
apis.example:
const bunPath = Bun.which("bun");
console.log(bunPath ?? "bun not found");

apis.name: Bun.sleep
apis.summary: Returns a promise that resolves after a number of milliseconds or at a given Date, without blocking the event loop.
apis.signature: Bun.sleep(ms: number | Date): Promise<void>
apis.example:
await Bun.sleep(100);
console.log("100ms later");

apis.name: Bun.sleepSync
apis.summary: Blocks the current thread for a number of milliseconds. Prefer Bun.sleep in async code.
apis.signature: Bun.sleepSync(ms: number): void
apis.example:
Bun.sleepSync(10);
console.log("blocked for 10ms");

apis.name: Bun.version
apis.summary: The Bun version string of the running runtime, for example "1.4.4".
apis.signature: Bun.version: string
apis.example:
console.log(`running bun ${Bun.version}`);
console.log(Bun.version_with_sha.startsWith(`v${Bun.version}`));

apis.name: Bun.nanoseconds
apis.summary: Returns a high-resolution monotonic timestamp in nanoseconds, useful for benchmarking.
apis.signature: Bun.nanoseconds(): number

apis.name: Bun.gc
apis.summary: Forces the JavaScriptCore garbage collector to run, optionally synchronously. Mostly useful in tests and benchmarks.
apis.signature: Bun.gc(force?: boolean): void
apis.example:
Bun.gc(true);
console.log("garbage collected");

apis.name: Bun.unsafe
apis.summary: Low-level helpers such as zero-copy byte-to-string conversion, GC aggression levels and memory footprint reporting. Intended for benchmarking and debugging, not daily code.
apis.signature: Bun.unsafe: { arrayBufferToString(buffer: Uint8Array | ArrayBufferLike): string; gcAggressionLevel(level?: 0 | 1 | 2): 0 | 1 | 2; memoryFootprint(): number | undefined; mimallocDump(): void }

apis.name: Bun.secrets
apis.summary: Stores and retrieves credentials in the operating system's secure storage: Keychain on macOS, libsecret on Linux and Credential Manager on Windows.
apis.signature: Bun.secrets: { get(options: { service: string; name: string }): Promise<string | null>; set(options: { service: string; name: string; value: string }): Promise<void>; delete(options: { service: string; name: string }): Promise<boolean> }

apis.name: Bun.embeddedFiles
apis.summary: The list of Blob files embedded in a standalone executable produced by bun build --compile. Empty in normal Bun runs.
apis.signature: Bun.embeddedFiles: readonly Blob[]

apis.name: Bun.cron
apis.summary: Schedules an in-process cron job that calls a handler on a five-field schedule or nickname. The returned job exposes cron, ref(), unref() and stop().
apis.signature: Bun.cron(schedule: string, handler: () => unknown, options?: Bun.CronOptions): Bun.CronJob

apis.name: Bun.isStandaloneExecutable
apis.summary: True when the current process is a standalone executable produced by bun build --compile, false when running under the bun binary.
apis.signature: Bun.isStandaloneExecutable: boolean
apis.example:
console.log("standalone:", Bun.isStandaloneExecutable);
console.log("embedded files:", Bun.embeddedFiles.length);

apis.name: Bun.ModuleGraph
apis.summary: Experimental isolated module graph: loads a module into the current process again with its own module instances, require.cache, injected globals and a timers/I/O context, while sharing parsed and JIT-compiled code. dispose() closes everything the graph opened and makes further import() and run() fail; it separates instances of an app you trust and is not a security sandbox.

apis.name: Bun.$
apis.summary: Runs shell commands with Bun Shell using tagged template literals. Returns a shell result whose text(), json(), quiet() and exit code you can consume.
apis.signature: Bun.$(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...expressions: Bun.ShellExpression[]): BunShell
apis.example:
const result = await Bun.$`echo "Hello, world!"`.text();
console.log(result.trim());

apis.name: Bun.spawn
apis.summary: Starts a child process asynchronously and returns a Subprocess handle with stdin, stdout, stderr, exited and kill().
apis.signature: Bun.spawn<In extends Bun.SpawnOptions.Writable = "ignore", Out extends Bun.SpawnOptions.Readable = "pipe", Err extends Bun.SpawnOptions.Readable = "inherit">(options: Bun.SpawnOptions.SpawnOptions<In, Out, Err>): Bun.Subprocess<In, Out, Err>

apis.name: Bun.spawnSync
apis.summary: Runs a child process synchronously and returns its exit code plus captured stdout and stderr buffers.
apis.signature: Bun.spawnSync<In extends Bun.SpawnOptions.Writable = "ignore", Out extends Bun.SpawnOptions.Readable = "pipe", Err extends Bun.SpawnOptions.Readable = "pipe">(options: Bun.SpawnOptions.SpawnSyncOptions<In, Out, Err>): Bun.SyncSubprocess<In, Out, Err>
apis.example:
const { stdout, exitCode } = Bun.spawnSync(["bun", "--version"]);
console.log(exitCode, stdout.toString().trim());

apis.name: Bun.Terminal
apis.summary: Creates a pseudo-terminal (PTY) that a spawned process can use as its terminal, so interactive programs get a real TTY. Supports write(), resize() and setRawMode().
apis.signature: class Bun.Terminal { constructor(options: Bun.TerminalOptions); write(data: string | BufferSource): number; resize(cols: number, rows: number): void; setRawMode(enabled: boolean): void }

apis.name: Bun.hash
apis.summary: Hashes a string or buffer with the fast non-cryptographic wyhash algorithm and returns a bigint. An optional seed changes the result.
apis.signature: Bun.hash(data: string | ArrayBufferView | ArrayBuffer | SharedArrayBuffer, seed?: number | bigint): bigint

apis.name: Bun.CryptoHasher
apis.summary: Incremental cryptographic hasher supporting the algorithms of node:crypto, including HMAC when a key is supplied. update() feeds data and digest() finalizes.
apis.signature: class Bun.CryptoHasher { constructor(algorithm: Bun.SupportedCryptoAlgorithms, hmacKey?: string | NodeJS.TypedArray); update(input: Bun.BlobOrStringOrBuffer, inputEncoding?: string): Bun.CryptoHasher; digest(encoding?: Bun.DigestEncoding): string; copy(): Bun.CryptoHasher }

apis.name: Bun.sha
apis.summary: Hashes input with SHA-512/256 and returns either the raw digest bytes or an encoded string such as hex or base64.
apis.signature: Bun.sha(input: Bun.StringOrBuffer, encoding: Bun.DigestEncoding): string
apis.example:
console.log(Bun.sha("hello world", "hex"));
console.log(Bun.sha("hello world", "base64"));

apis.name: Bun.password
apis.summary: Hashes and verifies passwords with argon2 or bcrypt, choosing and tuning the algorithm with an options object. Hash strings are stored in PHC or Modular Crypt Format.
apis.signature: Bun.password.hash(password: Bun.StringOrBuffer, options?: { algorithm?: "argon2id" | "argon2i" | "argon2d" | "bcrypt"; memoryCost?: number; timeCost?: number; cost?: number }): Promise<string>
apis.example:
const hash = await Bun.password.hash("hunter2", { algorithm: "argon2id" });
console.log(await Bun.password.verify("hunter2", hash));

apis.name: Bun.randomUUIDv7
apis.summary: Generates a time-ordered UUIDv7 that sorts chronologically, encoded as hex, base64, base64url or a Buffer.
apis.signature: Bun.randomUUIDv7(encoding?: "hex" | "base64" | "base64url", timestamp?: number | Date): string

apis.name: Bun.randomUUIDv5
apis.summary: Generates a deterministic name-based UUIDv5 from a name and a namespace UUID (or one of the predefined dns, url, oid, x500 namespaces).
apis.signature: Bun.randomUUIDv5(name: string | BufferSource, namespace: string | BufferSource | "dns" | "url" | "oid" | "x500", encoding?: "hex" | "base64" | "base64url"): string
apis.example:
const id = Bun.randomUUIDv5("example.com", "dns");
console.log(id);

apis.name: Bun.CSRF
apis.summary: Generates and verifies CSRF tokens signed with HMAC. Each token embeds a nonce, an issue timestamp and an expiry duration.
apis.signature: Bun.CSRF: { generate(secret?: string, options?: Bun.CSRFGenerateOptions): string; verify(token: string, options?: Bun.CSRFVerifyOptions): boolean }
apis.example:
const token = Bun.CSRF.generate("my-secret");
console.log(Bun.CSRF.verify(token, { secret: "my-secret" }));

apis.name: Bun.gzipSync
apis.summary: Compresses data with the gzip format synchronously and returns a Uint8Array. Accepts optional zlib/libdeflate compression options.
apis.signature: Bun.gzipSync(data: Uint8Array | string | ArrayBuffer, options?: Bun.ZlibCompressionOptions | Bun.LibdeflateCompressionOptions): Uint8Array

apis.name: Bun.gunzipSync
apis.summary: Decompresses gzip data synchronously and returns the original bytes as a Uint8Array.
apis.signature: Bun.gunzipSync(data: Uint8Array | string | ArrayBuffer, options?: Bun.ZlibCompressionOptions | Bun.LibdeflateCompressionOptions): Uint8Array
apis.example:
const gz = Bun.gzipSync("hello world");
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(Bun.gunzipSync(gz)));

apis.name: Bun.deflateSync
apis.summary: Compresses data with the raw zlib DEFLATE algorithm synchronously. Pair it with Bun.inflateSync to decompress.
apis.signature: Bun.deflateSync(data: Uint8Array | string | ArrayBuffer, options?: Bun.ZlibCompressionOptions | Bun.LibdeflateCompressionOptions): Uint8Array
apis.example:
const compressed = Bun.deflateSync("hello world");
console.log(compressed.byteLength, new TextDecoder().decode(Bun.inflateSync(compressed)));

apis.name: Bun.inflateSync
apis.summary: Decompresses raw DEFLATE data synchronously back into the original bytes.
apis.signature: Bun.inflateSync(data: Uint8Array | string | ArrayBuffer, options?: Bun.ZlibCompressionOptions | Bun.LibdeflateCompressionOptions): Uint8Array
apis.example:
const compressed = Bun.deflateSync("hello world");
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(Bun.inflateSync(compressed)));

apis.name: Bun.zstdCompress
apis.summary: Compresses data with Zstandard asynchronously and resolves to a Buffer. An optional level tunes the compression ratio.
apis.signature: Bun.zstdCompress(data: NodeJS.TypedArray | Buffer | string | ArrayBuffer, options?: { level?: number }): Promise<Buffer>
apis.example:
const compressed = await Bun.zstdCompress("hello world");
console.log((await Bun.zstdDecompress(compressed)).toString());

apis.name: Bun.zstdDecompress
apis.summary: Decompresses Zstandard data asynchronously and resolves to a Buffer.
apis.signature: Bun.zstdDecompress(data: NodeJS.TypedArray | Buffer | string | ArrayBuffer): Promise<Buffer>
apis.example:
const compressed = await Bun.zstdCompress("hello");
console.log((await Bun.zstdDecompress(compressed)).toString());

apis.name: Bun.Archive
apis.summary: Creates and extracts tar archives, optionally gzip-compressed, from an object of file contents or existing archive bytes. files(), bytes() and blob() read an archive in memory while extract() writes it to a directory.
apis.signature: class Bun.Archive { constructor(data: Bun.ArchiveInput, options?: Bun.ArchiveOptions); extract(path: string, options?: Bun.ArchiveExtractOptions): Promise<number>; files(glob?: string | readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, File>>; bytes(): Promise<Uint8Array>; blob(): Promise<Blob> }

apis.name: Bun.inspect
apis.summary: Formats any value as a readable string the way console.log does, including colors and depth options. Handy for logging and diagnostics.
apis.signature: Bun.inspect(value: unknown, options?: Bun.BunInspectOptions): string
apis.example:
const formatted = Bun.inspect({ a: 1, b: [2, 3] }, { colors: false });
console.log(formatted);

apis.name: Bun.deepEquals
apis.summary: Compares two values deeply for equality. With strict set to true, object prototypes and types must also match.
apis.signature: Bun.deepEquals(a: unknown, b: unknown, strict?: boolean): boolean
apis.example:
console.log(Bun.deepEquals({ a: 1 }, { a: 1 }));
console.log(Bun.deepEquals([1, 2], [2, 1]));

apis.name: Bun.escapeHTML
apis.summary: Escapes the characters that are unsafe in HTML text and attributes: &, <, >, ", and '.
apis.signature: Bun.escapeHTML(input: string | object | number | boolean): string
apis.example:
const safe = Bun.escapeHTML("<script>alert('x')</script>");
console.log(safe);

apis.name: Bun.stripANSI
apis.summary: Removes ANSI escape sequences from a string, leaving only the visible text.
apis.signature: Bun.stripANSI(input: string): string
apis.example:
const plain = Bun.stripANSI("\u001b[31mred\u001b[0m");
console.log(plain);

apis.name: Bun.stringWidth
apis.summary: Counts how many terminal columns a string occupies, accounting for wide CJK characters and emoji. ANSI codes can be counted or ignored.
apis.signature: Bun.stringWidth(input: string, options?: Bun.StringWidthOptions): number
apis.example:
console.log(Bun.stringWidth("hello"));
console.log(Bun.stringWidth("你好"));

apis.name: Bun.wrapAnsi
apis.summary: Wraps text to a maximum column width while preserving ANSI escape sequences across line breaks.
apis.signature: Bun.wrapAnsi(input: string, columns: number, options?: Bun.WrapAnsiOptions): string
apis.example:
const wrapped = Bun.wrapAnsi("The quick brown fox", 10);
console.log(wrapped);

apis.name: Bun.sliceAnsi
apis.summary: Slices a string by visible column width, keeping ANSI escape sequences valid. Supports negative indexes and an ellipsis for truncation.
apis.signature: Bun.sliceAnsi(input: string, start?: number, end?: number, options?: string | boolean | Bun.SliceAnsiOptions): string
apis.example:
console.log(Bun.sliceAnsi("hello world", 0, 5));
console.log(Bun.sliceAnsi("hello world", -5));

apis.name: Bun.SQL
apis.summary: A SQL client for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite that is also callable as a tagged template. It manages a connection pool and exposes close() and transaction helpers.
apis.signature: class Bun.SQL { constructor(connectionString: string | URL, options?: Bun.SQL.Options); <T = unknown>(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]): Promise<T[]>; close(): Promise<void> }

apis.name: bun:sqlite Database
apis.summary: The built-in SQLite3 database class from the bun:sqlite module. Supports prepared statements, transactions and synchronous queries.
apis.signature: new Database(filename?: string, options?: { readonly?: boolean; create?: boolean; readwrite?: boolean; safeIntegers?: boolean; strict?: boolean }): Database

apis.name: Bun.RedisClient
apis.summary: A Redis (and Valkey) client with promise-based get/set/del, hashes, pub/sub and pipeline support. The URL defaults to VALKEY_URL, REDIS_URL or localhost.
apis.signature: new Bun.RedisClient(url?: string, options?: Bun.RedisOptions): Bun.RedisClient

apis.name: Bun.S3Client
apis.summary: An S3-compatible bucket client. file() returns an S3File for reading and writing objects, and presign(), list(), delete(), size() and exists() cover the common operations.
apis.signature: new Bun.S3Client(options?: Bun.S3Options): Bun.S3Client

apis.name: Bun.TOML
apis.summary: Parses TOML documents into objects and serializes objects back to TOML. Date/time values become Temporal objects.
apis.signature: Bun.TOML: { parse(input: string | NodeJS.TypedArray | Blob): object; stringify(input: unknown, replacer?: null, space?: string | number): string }

apis.name: Bun.YAML
apis.summary: Parses YAML documents, including multi-document streams, anchors, aliases and cyclic anchors, and serializes JavaScript values back to YAML; cyclic values stringify as anchors and aliases.
apis.signature: Bun.YAML: { parse(input: string | NodeJS.TypedArray | Blob): unknown; stringify(value: unknown, replacer?: null, space?: string | number): string }

apis.name: Bun.JSON5
apis.summary: Parses and serializes JSON5, the JSON superset that allows comments, trailing commas, unquoted keys and single-quoted strings.
apis.signature: Bun.JSON5: { parse(input: string): unknown; stringify(value: unknown, replacer?: null, space?: string | number): string | undefined }
apis.example:
const value = Bun.JSON5.parse("{ name: 'bun', trailing: [1, 2,], }");
console.log(value.name, value.trailing.length);

apis.name: Bun.JSONL
apis.summary: Parses JSON Lines, where every line is one JSON value. parseChunk() is designed for streaming input and reports how many bytes were consumed.
apis.signature: Bun.JSONL: { parse(input: string | NodeJS.TypedArray): unknown[]; parseChunk(input: string | NodeJS.TypedArray, start?: number, end?: number): { values: unknown[]; read: number; done: boolean; error: SyntaxError | null } }
apis.example:
const rows = Bun.JSONL.parse('{"a":1}\n{"a":2}\n');
console.log(rows.length, rows[1].a);

apis.name: Bun.XML
apis.summary: Parses XML into a compact object shape (attributes as @name keys, text as #text) and serializes values back to XML.
apis.signature: Bun.XML: { parse(input: string | NodeJS.TypedArray | Blob, options?: Bun.XML.ParseOptions): Bun.XML.Document | Bun.XML.Node; stringify(value: unknown, replacer?: null, space?: string | number): string | undefined }
apis.example:
const doc = Bun.XML.parse("<root><item>hello</item></root>");
console.log(doc.root.item);

apis.name: Bun.markdown
apis.summary: Renders Markdown with GitHub-flavored extensions to HTML, to ANSI terminal output, or through custom render callbacks; a React helper is also available.
apis.signature: Bun.markdown: { html(input: string, options?: Bun.markdown.Options): string; ansi(input: string, theme?: Bun.markdown.AnsiTheme): string; render(input: string, callbacks?: Bun.markdown.RenderCallbacks, options?: Bun.markdown.Options): string; react(input: string, components?: unknown): unknown }
apis.example:
const html = Bun.markdown.html("# Hello **world**");
console.log(html.trim());

apis.name: Bun.build
apis.summary: Bundles JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, CSS and HTML entrypoints into optimized outputs using Bun's native bundler. Resolves to a BuildOutput with success, outputs and logs.
apis.signature: Bun.build(config: Bun.BuildConfig): Promise<Bun.BuildOutput>

apis.name: Bun.Transpiler
apis.summary: Transpiles TypeScript, JSX and modern JavaScript to current JavaScript in memory without bundling or resolving imports. `scan()` returns the module's exports and imports with metadata, and `scanImports()` is the faster imports-only variant; type-only imports and exports are ignored.
apis.signature: class Bun.Transpiler { constructor(options?: Bun.TranspilerOptions); transformSync(code: Bun.StringOrBuffer, loader?: Bun.Loader): string; transform(code: Bun.StringOrBuffer, loader?: Bun.Loader): Promise<string>; scan(code: Bun.StringOrBuffer): { exports: string[]; imports: Bun.Import[] }; scanImports(code: Bun.StringOrBuffer): Bun.Import[] }

apis.name: Bun.plugin
apis.summary: Registers a plugin that can intercept module resolution and loading at runtime, used to import and transform custom file types.
apis.signature: Bun.plugin(plugin: Bun.BunPlugin): void

apis.name: Bun.resolve
apis.summary: Resolves a module specifier as if it were imported from a parent path, using Bun's module resolution. The synchronous twin is Bun.resolveSync().
apis.signature: Bun.resolve(moduleId: string, parent: string): Promise<string>
apis.example:
const path = await Bun.resolve("./package.json", process.cwd());
console.log(path);

apis.name: Bun.FFI
apis.summary: Foreign-function interface for calling native libraries from JavaScript. dlopen() loads a shared library, maps its symbols and returns typed call wrappers.
apis.signature: Bun.FFI: { dlopen(path: string, symbols: Record<string, Bun.FFIFunction>): { symbols: Bun.FFIFunctionCallable; close(): void }; callback(fn: Function, definition: Bun.FFIFunction): unknown; linkSymbols(symbols: Record<string, Bun.FFIFunction>): { symbols: Bun.FFIFunctionCallable }; CString(value: string): unknown; ptr(value: unknown): unknown }
